newsitem.title: KENYA: Rates marginally lower on Kenya's main T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Rates marginally lower on Kenya's main T-bills.

text.p: Interest rates were a touch lower on Kenya's main stock of treasury bills at the auction on Thursday, the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) said on Friday.
It posted the average yield on 91-day treasury bills at 20.900 percent compared to 20.991 percent last week.
The yield on the second category 28-day treasury bills was 16.498 percent compared to 16.5000 percent last week.

The central bank tendered 10.187 billion shillings ($188.64 million) in 91-day T-bills, of which 9.463 billion was accepted. Only 125 million shillings in 28-day bills was tendered and all was accepted, according to central bank figures.

There were 177 bids for 91-day T-bills of which 105 were successful, 30 non-successful and 42 non-competitive. There were five bids for 28-day T-bills, of which four were successful and one was non-competitive, the central bank said.

The central bank posted redemptions for the week at 11.485 billion shillings for 91-day T-bills and 524 million for 28-day T-bills. The bank invited tenders for T-bills worth seven billion shillings for the auction next Thursday.
